summary.text: 高 is a pictograph traditionally interpreted as a tall building or raised tower; it represents the idea of being high or tall. Today it commonly means “high” or “tall.”

formation.text: Pictographic: the whole graph depicts a tall structure, understood in the traditional account as a raised building or viewing tower. The traditional breakdown into 冂 and 口 is a historical analysis, not evidence that these are independently meaningful parts of the original picture.

components.text: The graph is best explained as one picture of a tall structure. A traditional dictionary analysis separates it into 冂 and 口, but their separate original meanings and roles are not established; they are not treated here as independent components.

history.text: Catalogues record forms of 高 in oracle-bone and bronze inscriptions, as well as later scripts. The available descriptions support a broad graphic history but do not establish specific changes between those forms; the early examples’ lexical contexts are also not verified here.
高 is compared graphically with 京, another character described as depicting a tall structure. The resemblance does not establish that one derives from the other or that 京 is a component of 高.
The standard form is 高; 髙 is recorded as a variant.

uncertainties.text: The tower interpretation is supported, but the exact architecture depicted and the earliest securely established word sense remain unresolved in this evidence. The traditional analysis using 冂 and 口 does not establish separate original contributions for those shapes.

The evidence does not establish a graphic or lexical relationship between 高 and 京, nor a definite lexical relationship between 高 and 喬. No phonetic component or whole-character borrowing is proposed here.

senses.text: The traditional pictographic interpretation connects the tall structure with the idea “high.” No verified inscription context in this dossier securely establishes this as the earliest attested lexical sense.
The common current meaning is “high” or “tall.”

senses.gloss: high place or ridge; excellence, esteem, high price, old age, or a high/forceful voice
senses.text: Textual citations and dictionary records attest these uses, but do not establish when they arose or how they developed from “high/tall.” Their pathways are therefore left unspecified.

limitations.text: Although the traditional account links a tall-building picture to “high,” the earliest lexical sense and the chronology of that connection are not securely established by a dated inscription context here.
The evidence lists historical uses such as “excellent,” “esteemed,” “expensive,” “old,” and “loud,” but does not establish their dates or semantic pathways.

overview.text: Think of 高 as one picture of a tall structure, used for the idea “high” or “tall.” The traditional account supports this interpretation, though the earliest word sense is not securely dated here.

components.text: Read the whole graph as a tall structure. The traditional split into 冂 and 口 does not establish separate meanings for those shapes.
